scope.frame: B1656's four-channel coupling (the functions B1723 sealed) with a flavour-blind Higgs S = 1
scope.object: the singular values of Y = c 1 + [a]_x, the coupling in every sector for every line, tau, end and channel weighting
scope.hypotheses: none beyond the frame: c in C and a in C^3 arbitrary; the premise computed on 20 random weightings, the bound proved

claim_one_line: THE FLAVOUR-BLIND BOUND (P-299; proved, no data): with a flavour-blind Higgs S = 1, B1656's coupling is linear in the four channel weights and gives in every sector Y = c 1 + [a]_x (the channel 1 gives the identity, i, j, k the three elementary antisymmetric matrices; to 2.5e-16), whatever the line, tau and end; and for every c in C and a in C^3 the singular values satisfy sigma_1 <= 3 sigma_2, so m2/m3 >= 1/3, sharp (equality at c = 1, a = 2i e_1, singular values 3, 1, 1) -- by Weyl's inequalities, since M + M^T = 2c 1 gives |c| <= sigma_2 and the antisymmetric part has sigma_1 = sigma_2; the minimum by 400 starts 0.333333333333, every step on 200 000 random draws without violation. The data (m_c/m_t ~ 0.0037, m_s/m_b ~ 0.02, m_mu/m_tau ~ 0.06) lie far below, so in this frame the charged-fermion hierarchy needs a flavoured Higgs. 0 of 19.
weave_or_thread: weave (a property of the frame's coupling at every tau and line)
